title: claude-md-harness-rules
desc: How to configure per-repo harness rules in CLAUDE.md: harness:safe/block/warn/done/skill syntax, tInput format, body lines, template injection. Includes the harness:skill study-lock (principle/implementation/usage): isEditOp recognition, file-path-only patterns, 4-condition block matrix, executed-read detection.
steps: WHAT: Per-repo CLAUDE.md declarative rules that the harness (wkharness-guards.ps1) enforces on every tool call. Parsed at session start from the project CLAUDE.md.
SYNTAX: One rule = one ## header line + optional body lines. Header: '## harness:<action> <regex>'. Body: plain text shown in message; lines starting with ! run as PowerShell and output is appended.
ACTIONS: safe = whitelist (skip all block/warn if tInput matches). block = Block() the tool call with message. warn = write to stderr (no block). done = PostToolUse only (completion detector).
tInput FORMAT: '● ToolName(cmd)' -- e.g. '● Bash(rm -rf /tmp/foo)' or '● Edit(CLAUDE.md)'. Regex matches against this string. Anchor with '● Bash\(' to avoid false positives on tool args.
EXAMPLES: ## harness:safe CLAUDE\.md  (allow Edit on CLAUDE.md always)
## harness:block (?i)● Bash\(.*rm -rf  (block dangerous rm)
## harness:warn (?i)● Bash\(.*sed -i  (warn on sed)
## harness:done (?i)completed
done  (PostToolUse completion check)
BODY LINES: Plain text = shown as help message. Line starting with ! = PowerShell command, output inserted. E.g.: !wkappbot skill read wk-ai-tools  (shows skill content in block message)
TEMPLATE: If CLAUDE.md has no harness: sections, ~/.claude/harness-template.md is auto-appended. Template has 4 default rules (safe CLAUDE.md, warn wkedit--line, block bash-pwsh, done skipped).
SCOPE: Only the CWD project CLAUDE.md is loaded (not global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md). Each repo controls its own rules. Global rules live in wkharness-guards.ps1 hardcoded guards.

BEST PRACTICES: Use safe before block to whitelist exceptions. Anchor block patterns to '● Bash\(' or '● Edit\(' to avoid matching tool arguments. Keep regex simple -- no lookahead. Test with wkharness -Test.

ACTION 'skill' (study-lock) -- PRINCIPLE: force the editor to actually STUDY the relevant skills BEFORE editing a matching source file, so nobody blindly edits sensitive code (placement, screensaver, caller-hwnd, etc.). IMPLEMENTATION: (i) the guard recognizes OFFICIAL EDIT commands via isEditOp = Edit/Write tool OR Bash/PS starting with wkedit/wkcodex/wkclaude or containing 'wkappbot file edit'; Read/Grep are NOT edit ops so they never block. (ii) the harness:skill PATTERN is FILE-PATH-ONLY (e.g. csharp.*MyCdpContext) -- NO Edit-open-paren prefix; the guard CODE decides the tool, the MD entry only says which files. (iii) 4-condition BLOCK matrix: A edit-op recognized; B edit-op on a source file whose path matches NO harness:skill pattern -> catch-all block (guides you to add a section); C pattern matched but the entry declares fewer than 3 distinct skill ids -> bad-config block; D pattern matched but not ALL declared skills were READ this session -> block listing the unread ones. (iv) read = an actual EXECUTED 'wkappbot skill read id' command found in the session JSONL (lines carrying a Bash/PS command field, whole-session, no recency limit) -- plain-text mentions (the rule text itself, skill Require lines, prose) do NOT count; agent/wkcodex reads DO count. Block message goes to stderr.

ACTION 'skill' USAGE -- declare in CLAUDE.md: a header '## harness:skill <FILE-PATH-REGEX>' followed by exactly 3+ body lines of the form 'wkappbot skill read <id>' (convention: usage / impl / task). Example: '## harness:skill csharp.*MyCdpContext' then 'wkappbot skill read standard-appbot-window' / 'wkappbot skill read standard-chrome-window' / 'wkappbot skill read wkfind-caller-hwnd-validation-3tier-pattern'. Rules: the 3 skill ids MUST exist in the catalog and be distinct (else condition C bad-config block); the pattern is matched against the normalized edited-file path, so write just the path fragment (no Edit-open-paren). To pass before editing a matching file, EXECUTE those 3 'wkappbot skill read' commands this session (text-only mention does not satisfy it). If you edit an unregistered source file, the catch-all (condition B) blocks and prints the exact '## harness:skill ext.*Filename' section to add. NOTE: this is separate from the skill-update LOCK (code_changed...lock) which is cleared by any 'wkappbot skill edit/contribute' and gates the NEXT delegation wrapper/Agent.

CORRECTION to the isEditOp scope (overrides the earlier list): detect ONLY explicit DIRECT edits -- the Edit and Write tools, plus appbot-edit Bash commands (wkappbot file edit / wkedit). Do NOT include wkcodex / wkclaude in isEditOp: those are delegation wrappers, not direct edits, and they are already gated by the brief-guard (3 skill-read refs in the task). Including them caused false skill-query triggers when a wkcodex task string merely MENTIONS a registered file path. So: isEditOp = (tool is Edit or Write) OR (Bash/PS command is wkappbot-file-edit or wkedit). Reads/greps/other Bash never trigger the skill query.

GLOBAL CLAUDE.md INTEGRATION (requirement): in addition to the CWD project CLAUDE.md (and the edited-file repo-root CLAUDE.md cross-repo pass), the harness should ALSO load and apply the GLOBAL user CLAUDE.md at HOME/.claude/CLAUDE.md so user-level harness rules apply in every repo. IMPLEMENTATION in wkharness.ps1 right after the main 'Invoke-HarnessRules cfg toolName harnessInput pre' call: add globalMd = Join-Path USERPROFILE '.claude/CLAUDE.md'; if Test-Path globalMd then Invoke-HarnessRules (Get-HarnessRules globalMd) toolName harnessInput 'pre' with skipEditCatchAll=true (true so the global pass does NOT re-fire the source-edit catch-all -- only the CWD pass owns the catch-all). Order: CWD project rules first, then edited-file repo rules, then global rules; safe/block/warn/skill all merge. This complements step 12 which previously said only CWD is loaded.

GLOBAL CLAUDE.md integration -- self-test safety: gate the global-load with (-not env:WKHARNESS_SELFTEST) so the 72 deterministic self-test cases (which assume only the controlled CWD fixture rules) are NOT affected by the real user-level rules; real sessions still get the global pass. The global Invoke-HarnessRules call mirrors the existing edited-file cross-repo pass (skipEditCatchAll true).

IMPLEMENTED SOLUTION (2026-05-27, FINAL -- supersedes the isEditOp guard-code idea above): the edit-tool / appbot-edit discrimination is done ENTIRELY in the harness:skill PATTERN, NOT in guard code. No isEditOp is needed. This is clobber-IMMUNE because it lives in the project CLAUDE.md (which is pace-exempt to edit), not in the concurrently-edited wkharness-guards.ps1. Canonical pattern prefix: (?:Edit\(|Write\(|Bash\((?:[\w./\-]+\s+)*?[\w./\-]*edit(?:\.\w+)?\b) then .*<ext>.*<FileFragment>. Coverage proven live: Edit tool (Edit\(), Write tool (Write\(), and any Bash command whose command-position token ends in 'edit' -- wkedit, wkedit.sh/.ps1/.cmd/.exe, 'wkappbot file edit', even with leading flags like --sudo or --timeout 30s (each flag/value is absorbed by the leading-token group). Reads/Greps never match (no Edit(/Write(/Bash(...edit token). wkcodex/wkclaude tasks are excluded because their 'edit' mention sits inside a quoted arg and the quote stops the unquoted-token traversal. To register a file: ## harness:skill <thatPrefix>.*csharp.*MyCdpContext + 3 wkappbot skill read lines.

Edit/Write TOOL bypasses harness:skill: confirmed via controlled test -- Bash appbot-edit on .ps1 BLOCKS, but Edit TOOL on same .ps1 PASSES. Cause: an early exit-0 in wkharness-guards.ps1 short-circuits Edit/Write before the harness eval (~line 1430). Fix must ensure harness:skill/catch-all runs for Edit/Write tool too.

Lock clears on a clean update, but a command whose text carries a wrapper-name literal gets mis-tagged by the post-hook and re-arms the lock. Keep update text free of such literals to clear the lock for delegation.

Lock-clear hygiene: a clearing update must carry no wrapper-tool name token anywhere in its full command line (skill id and message body included) or the post-hook mis-tags it and re-arms. Run the delegated dispatch as the very next call with no shell or version-control command in between.

UPDATE (commit 53feb82): the skill-lock self-rearm Catch-22 is RESOLVED. wkappbot skill edit no longer arms the lock because the post-hook now verb-anchors source-edit detection and excludes skill catalog ops (skill edit/contribute/add). The earlier clean-text-only hygiene guidance is obsolete -- a normal skill edit clears the lock and it stays clear, so delegation via wkcodex works right after.

harness:skill pattern prefix RULE: always use the robust prefix (?:Edit\(|Write\(|Bash\((?:[\w./\-]+\s+)*?[\w./\-]*edit(?:\.\w+)?\b).* before the target match. The old Edit\(.* prefix matches only the Edit tool, so the Write tool and Bash appbot-edit/wkedit bypass the lock. Input is normalized backslash-to-slash before matching, so target matches like .*csharp.*MyCdpContext are slash-agnostic (mixed slashes are safe). Coverage snapshot 2026-05-27: WKAppBot 8 specific + source catch-all; wkappbot-sdk Launcher placement + EyeCmdPipe + source catch-all; WkAutoQuant 17 trading sources (prefix upgraded); personal-docs wkharness.

TIER0/1/2 EXEMPTION LADDER (2026-06-10, implemented in wkharness-guards.ps1): isKnowledgeOp() + isHarnessSourceEdit() helpers are the single source of truth. TIER0 = always-allow, never counted in stall = { Skill tool; wkappbot skill read/search/list/edit/contribute/news; Edit/Write of any .md file }. TIER1 = harness-source edits (wkharness*.ps1) = study-lock check only. READ-ONLY built-ins (Read/Glob/Grep/LS/Todo*/Task*) = stall-counted + stall-blockable, but exempt from pace and wk-only. TIER2 = everything else = all guards apply. SACRED principle: knowledge-ification and harness self-repair must NEVER be blockable -- an AI must always be able to read/edit skills and .md files to escape any guard cascade.

SKILL-LOCK SOURCE REFERENCES -- no marker line needed, auto-detected, and SCATTERABLE by location (2026-06-10 spec, user). A source file does NOT need a '#/// harness:skill' MARKER header. The harness study-lock AUTO-DETECTS every 'wkappbot skill read <id>' pattern appearing ANYWHERE in the source and aggregates them all into the lock. Consequences: (a) DROP the redundant '#/// harness:skill' header line; (b) place each 'wkappbot skill read <id>' reference SEPARATELY at the exact LOCATION where that skill is relevant -- e.g. the regex-hoist skill ref immediately above the regex-hoist function, the symbol-precheck skill ref above that function -- and the lock still recognizes + collects them all. This is more elegant than a single header block: each skill reference lives next to the code it governs, so an AI editing near that code is locked to exactly the right skill, not a generic top-of-file list. Also a commit-hygiene lesson learned the same day: path-limiting a commit (git commit -- file) is NOT enough -- the path-limited file can itself carry pre-existing uncommitted changes (e.g. a colleague's in-progress refactor) that get swept in; ALWAYS run 'git diff --cached' and read it before committing a shared-repo source file.

GEMINI DYNAMIC-DENY WORKS -- the path to hard-enforce + clean UX (VERIFIED 2026-06-11). Adding a rule to ~/.gemini/policies/autonomy.toml -- [[rule]] toolName=<tool> decision=deny priority=2000 (> the global allow priority 1000) -- ACTUALLY ENFORCES the block for a gemini session. Proof: a forced flash agent ran its shell command (allowed -> file created) but its write_file was BLOCKED (file absent) -- clean disambiguation. Each Agent.cmd-spawned model is a NEW session that reads autonomy.toml fresh (user insight), so the deny applies. THIS RESOLVES the soft-warn-vs-enforce tradeoff from the hook-fix: instead of just translating exit-2 to exit-0 (which made gemini blocks soft-warns / tool-proceeds), the relay should on a gemini guard block ADD a scoped deny to autonomy.toml, THEN exit 0 -- giving HARD ENFORCEMENT (gemini denies via policy) AND a clean UX (no 'Hook failed', no fallback prompt). TODO (next budget): implement in D:/GitHub/wkharness.ps1 -- on kih exit 2 for the gemini/agy family, append a deny for that tool to autonomy.toml + exit 0, and clean the deny on the next BeforeTool (one-shot scope). CAVEAT untested: whether a deny added MID-session applies to the CURRENT call of an already-running gemini session (verified only for fresh spawned sessions). Related: the exit-2->0 hook-fix in wkharness.ps1 + wkharness-post.ps1 (Flash 'Hook failed' + prompt root cause = gemini reads non-zero exit as failure).

GEMINI AUTONOMY.TOML CONSTRAINTS (verified 2026-06-11 from bundle chunk-6ZHP2EJW.js): (1) priority MUST be 0-999 -- parser enforces max(999); priority>=1000 jumps to next tier and is REJECTED. v1 wkharness.ps1 used priority=2000 which FAILS validation silently (rule loads into wrong tier). Use priority=900 for user-injected deny. (2) commandPrefix + commandRegex can ONLY be used with toolName="run_shell_command" (SHELL_TOOL_NAMES=["run_shell_command","ShellTool"]); using them with other toolNames causes validation error. (3) argsPattern for file tools: stableStringify() wraps each top-level key-value pair with NUL chars (\x00), so the pattern for write_file file_path matching is: \x00"file_path":"<escaped-path>"\x00 (use \0 literal in toml argsPattern string since toml strings parse \0 as the literal NUL byte). (4) For agy tools: the policy engine sees the NATIVE gemini tool names (run_shell_command, write_file, replace) NOT the mapped Claude names, because mapping happens in the relay BEFORE passing to wkharness but the policy engine runs in the gemini process independently -- deny rules must use native gemini tool names.

GEMINI DYNAMIC-DENY v2 DESIGN (2026-06-11): Precise command-specific persistent deny vs v1 whole-tool one-shot. Architecture: (1) For run_shell_command: use commandPrefix = first token of command (e.g. "wkappbot file write" -> commandPrefix="wkappbot"). Rules: toolName="run_shell_command", commandPrefix="<cmd>", decision="deny", priority=900. (2) For write_file/replace: use argsPattern matching NUL-delimited stable-stringify format: pattern = "\x00\file_path\:\<escaped-path>\\x00". (3) DEDUP: before appending, scan existing rules for matching toolName+commandPrefix/argsPattern combo; skip if present. (4) PERSISTENT (not one-shot): precise rules survive across calls because they only deny the exact command/path, not the whole tool. SYMMETRIC APPROVE: function Remove-WkDenyRule(tool, cmdOrPath) scans [[rule]] blocks, matches toolName+commandPrefix/argsPattern, removes matching block. Triggered by env WKHARNESS_APPROVE="<tool>:<cmd>" before a BeforeTool call. (5) V1 FALLBACK (one-shot): when no command string derivable (tool_input is null/empty), fall back to whole-tool one-shot deny with WK-ONE-SHOT-DENY marker. Cleanup at top removes these next call. (6) MARKER NAMING: precise persistent rules use "# WK-PERSISTENT-DENY" (no cleanup); one-shot fallback uses "# WK-ONE-SHOT-DENY" (cleanup at top).

TOML argsPattern NUL-encoding (2026-06-11, investigation): buildParamArgsPattern returns a regex string "\\0\file_path\:\<value>\\\0" where \\0 is the regex pattern for matching a literal NUL byte (\x00). When gemini-cli writes this to autonomy.toml via its policy-persist path, it presumably writes argsPattern = "\u0000\file_path\:\<value>\\u0000" (TOML basic string with Unicode escape). In wkharness.ps1 we use a space surrogate " \file_path\:\<path>\ " as a placeholder in v2 initial impl -- INCORRECT. The correct TOML argsPattern value should match what buildParamArgsPattern generates: either use \u0000 TOML escape (if TOML parses it to NUL) or write raw NUL chars. Since TOML basic strings support \uXXXX: argsPattern = "\u0000\file_path\:\<escaped>\\u0000". This gets parsed to the regex string \x00"file_path":"<value>"\x00 which correctly matches the stableStringify output. The space-surrogate in v2 PS code is a bug -- must use \u0000 delimiters.

TOML argsPattern NUL-encoding (2026-06-11, investigation): buildParamArgsPattern returns a regex string "\\0\"file_path\":\"<value>\"\\0" where \\0 is the regex pattern for matching a literal NUL byte (\x00). When gemini-cli writes this to autonomy.toml via its policy-persist path, it presumably writes argsPattern = "\u0000\"file_path\":\"<value>\"\u0000" (TOML basic string with Unicode escape). In wkharness.ps1 we use a space surrogate " \"file_path\":\"<path>\" " as a placeholder in v2 initial impl -- INCORRECT. The correct TOML argsPattern value should match what buildParamArgsPattern generates: either use \u0000 TOML escape (if TOML parses it to NUL) or write raw NUL chars. Since TOML basic strings support \uXXXX: argsPattern = "\u0000\"file_path\":\"<escaped>\"\u0000". This gets parsed to the regex string \x00"file_path":"<value>"\x00 which correctly matches the stableStringify output. The space-surrogate in v2 PS code is a bug -- must use \u0000 delimiters.

argsPattern NUL impl: use PowerShell [char]0 to embed literal NUL in the TOML argsPattern string. The pattern must match stableStringify output which has literal NUL chars wrapping each top-level kv pair. In the TOML file, embed the actual NUL byte (byte 0x00) inside the argsPattern double-quoted string. This is simpler and more reliable than TOML Unicode escapes. PS code: $nul = [char]0; $argsPattern = "$nul`"file_path`":`"$escapedPath`"$nul". Then write this as: argsPattern = "$argsPattern" into the TOML file. The dedup check similarly compares with the NUL-embedded value. The Remove-WkDenyRule approve function also builds the match string the same way.

FAIL-CLOSED FOR THE CORE GUARD: study-lock integrity check at SESSION INIT (user 2026-06-12). The study-lock is THE core of the sustainable harness because it forces studying a skill before editing harness or source. So it must FAIL-CLOSED, never fail-open. DESIGN: at session start (the SessionStart wkdoctor run) execute a SYNTHETIC integrity canary that confirms the study-lock can actually FIRE -- part (a) Test-WkHarnessStudyLock returns true for an un-studied harness edit (classification plus non-empty required-set), and part (b) a STATIC scan finds NO bare catch-swallow of the study-lock Block in wkharness-guards.ps1 (the exact 2026-06-12 re-throw bug). If the canary FAILS, write the flag file under .claude/wkharness/study-lock-broken; the PreToolUse guard reads that flag at the TOP and HARD-BLOCKS every Edit or Write of a harness or source file with a study-lock-integrity message saying editing is forbidden until repaired. RATIONALE: a fail-OPEN core-enforcement guard equals silent un-gated editing, which is the incident where harness files were edited blind. The one guard whose job is to gate editing must NEVER let editing proceed while it is itself broken. Cross: verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static, incident-trauma-reflex-ref, harness-active-model-scoping.

STUDY-LOCK TARGETS MD-SPECIFIED PATTERNS, NOT JUST GIT-SOURCE (user 2026-06-12): a file matching a CLAUDE.md harness:skill rule pattern MUST be study-locked regardless of its file extension or whether it is git-tracked -- the MD-declared pattern is authoritative, the operator chose it. FIX: in Test-WkHarnessStudyLock (wkharness-common.ps1) the sourceExt early-return that skips non-source extensions must NOT skip a file that matches a harness:skill rule pattern or carries inline triple-slash skill markers; relax the gate so any rule-matched or inline-marked file proceeds, while the required-count-zero check still skips truly-unmatched files. Likewise the TIER2 declarative harness:skill engine must match by the MD pattern alone, not gate on a source-extension allowlist. RATIONALE: the operator declares which files are sensitive via the MD rule (config, data, non-source artifacts included); the study-lock must honor that declaration, not silently exempt a file just because its extension is not in a hardcoded source list. Cross: claude-md-harness-rules-ref, verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static.

CHEAP-AGENT SANDBOX-WRITE FREEDOM (2026-06-12). When a cheap-agent session (haiku codex flash etc) tries to edit a canonical harness file the harness-sandbox guard does not just block it -- it GRANTS write freedom to a sandbox copy. Allowed suffixes -proto -probe -yourmodel (haiku sonnet opus codex) -yourfamily (claude openai codex). Example edit wkharness-guards-proto.ps1 instead of wkharness-guards.ps1. Do full work in the sandbox copy. ROOT reviews and promotes the sandbox delta into canonical. Detector Test-WkHarnessSourceIsSandboxed in wkharness-common.ps1.

READ-TIME PROACTIVE NOTICE. When any session READS a harness or doctor ps1 file wkharness-post.ps1 emits two non-blocking stderr hints. One lists which skills must be read before editing this file. Two suggests the sandbox-suffix naming for cheap agents. Zero blocks happen on read. The study-lock block fires only at EDIT time and only if the required skills were not studied. So a cheap agent that reads first and studies the listed skills never hits a block. This is why reading before editing is the block-prevention path.

CONFIRMED 2026-06-12 subagent file permission boundary under harness-sandbox. A subagent even pro tier Sonnet CAN create a brand NEW harness file with no block but CANNOT edit an EXISTING canonical harness file which gets blocked and redirected to a -proto sandbox copy. Division of labor the subagent does ALL prep writes new helper files and writes exact final content into proto copies and reports it but the final MERGE into an existing canonical file is ROOT-only by construction not hoarding but a structural permission boundary. Efficient pattern delegate the full build with a verbatim spec let the sibling create new files plus proto copies then ROOT applies only the canonical edits a few keystrokes since content is already written and verified.

ROOT CAUSE the harness was BLIND to the model verified 2026-06-12. A nudge meant to change AI behavior must reach the MODEL context not just the user terminal. Two layers were broken. ONE the jisikhwa and agent-done nudges were emitted as plain Console Error WriteLine stderr which surfaces to the user terminal but NOT into the model context so the AI never received the knowledge-ification reminder after a delegation which is exactly why it appeared to never knowledge-ify on cue. The only channel that reaches the model is the PostToolUse hookSpecificOutput additionalContext JSON. TWO that additionalContext assembly used Join-String a PowerShell 7 only cmdlet but the hook runs Windows PowerShell 5.1 so it threw and the surrounding catch swallowed it meaning the ENTIRE additionalContext channel was dead and the model received nothing. The harness spoke into a channel the AI could not hear. FIX replaced Join-String with the 5.1-safe -join operator to revive the channel and routed the jisikhwa nudge into the additionalContext nudge context. RULE any nudge intended to steer the AI MUST flow through additionalContext not stderr and ALL hook code MUST be 5.1-safe no Join-String no SHA256 HashData no Split-String. Verify the model actually receives a nudge never assume stderr reaches it.
